key_insight: A NURBS-based level set framework enables CAD-compatible, uncertainty-aware topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff–Love shells without local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports material-efficient thin-shell designs under uncertain loads and material properties while retaining compatibility with CAD/CAM workflows.
method: Represent shell geometry and evolving material boundaries with NURBS-based isogeometric analysis and level sets.
Use the speed method for volume-form shape derivatives and a biharmonic equation to obtain descent directions.
Model uncertainty using Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian random fields.
evidence_signal: Single- and multi-patch numerical examples reproduce literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches, according to the abstract.
watch_item: Monte Carlo sampling may increase optimization cost; the abstract gives no sample counts or quantitative runtime comparisons.
paper_title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
